statement: The five letters of the word ORBIT are arranged in a row. In how many arrangements is neither vowel, O nor I, at either end of the row?

choices.misconception: I counted the ways to place O and I in the three middle places, 3 × 2, but forgot to arrange R, B and T in the other places.
I subtracted the arrangements with O at an end and those with I at an end, 48 each, from 120, but the arrangements with both vowels at the ends were taken away twice.
I only kept O away from the ends and forgot that I must stay away from the ends too.
I subtracted only the 12 arrangements with a vowel at both ends, but even one vowel at an end is not allowed.

hints: Deal with the restricted letters first.
The vowels must go into the three middle places. Count the ways to place O and I there, then the ways to arrange the three consonants in the places that are left, and multiply.
O has 3 middle places to choose from, then I has 2. The consonants R, B, T fill the remaining 3 places in $3! = 6$ ways.

solutions.reliable: Place the restricted letters first. O goes in one of the 3 middle places and I in one of the other 2: $3 \times 2 = 6$ ways. R, B and T fill the remaining three places, including both ends, in $3! = 6$ ways. Total $6 \times 6 = 36$. Check by complement: 120 arrangements, minus 48 with O at an end and 48 with I at an end, plus the 12 with both at the ends that were taken away twice: $120 - 96 + 12 = 36$. The transferable idea: in an arrangement with restrictions, place the most restricted objects first.
solutions.elegant: Fill the two ends with consonants in order: $3 \times 2 = 6$ ways. The remaining three letters fill the middle in $3! = 6$ ways: 36.

whyOnTest: Arrangements with restrictions reward placing the fussiest letters first; the distractors are the usual slips in the complement count.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
